title: Solar Panels in Las Cruces, NM: Cost, Savings & Local Guide (2026)
excerpt: Las Cruces gets 6.3+ peak sun hours daily — among the highest in the US. A 6kW solar system saves the average homeowner $950–1,100 per year with a payback period under 10 years.
content:
Why Las Cruces Is One of America's Best Solar Cities

Las Cruces, New Mexico sits in the Chihuahuan Desert at 3,900 feet elevation — a combination that produces exceptional solar conditions. The city averages 6.3 peak sun hours per day, which puts it in the top 5% of US cities for solar production. For comparison, the national average is about 4.5 hours. More sun hours means more electricity produced per panel, which directly shortens your payback period.

Solar Panel Cost in Las Cruces

A standard 6 kW residential solar system in Las Cruces costs $16,000–$20,000 before incentives. After applying the federal 30% Investment Tax Credit ($4,800–$6,000 back), your net cost is typically $11,000–$14,000. New Mexico also offers a state solar tax credit of up to $6,000 (10% of system cost, capped at $9,000 system value), which can reduce your cost further to as low as $8,000–$10,000 net.

Annual Savings and Payback Period

At El Paso Electric's current residential rates (Las Cruces is served by El Paso Electric, not PNM), a 6 kW system producing roughly 9,900 kWh per year saves approximately $950–$1,100 annually. At that savings rate, most Las Cruces homeowners break even in 8–11 years — well ahead of the 25-year panel warranty. Over 25 years, total savings typically reach $28,000–$35,000.

Las Cruces Utility: El Paso Electric Net Metering

El Paso Electric offers net metering to Las Cruces residential customers. Excess solar electricity you export to the grid earns you credits at the retail rate — currently around $0.128/kWh. This means overproduction in summer months (when your panels produce more than you use) offsets your bills in winter. EPE's net metering policy is rated among the better programs in the Southwest.

Local Solar Installers in Las Cruces

Las Cruces has a competitive installer market with both national companies (Sunrun, Tesla Energy, Palmetto) and strong regional firms serving the El Paso–Las Cruces corridor. Getting 3+ quotes is especially important here — installer pricing in Las Cruces varies by 15–25% for identical systems. Local installers who know EPE's interconnection process tend to have faster installation timelines than national firms.

Should You Go Solar in Las Cruces?

With a solar score of 95/100, Las Cruces is an exceptional solar market. The combination of extreme sun hours, New Mexico's state credit stacked on top of the federal credit, and EPE's net metering makes this one of the strongest ROI cases in the country. The main consideration is roof age — if your roof is over 15 years old, get a roofing assessment before signing a solar contract, since panel removal for a roof replacement costs $1,000–2,000 extra.
